Danish

Etymology

Originally the neuter of megen (“much”) (formal), but it is used with both genders in the contemporary language.

Pronunciation

  • IPA(key): /majəð/, [ˈmɑðð̩], (Jutlandish) IPA(key): /majət/, [ˈmɑɪd̥]

Adjective

meget

  1. neuter singular of megen

Determiner

meget (comparative mere, superlative mest)

  1. a lot of, much (preceding a noun)

See also

  • mange

Pronoun

meget

  1. much, a lot

Adverb

meget

  1. very
  2. much

References

  • “megen” in Den Danske Ordbog
  • “megen” in Ordbog over det danske Sprog

Norwegian Bokmål

Etymology

From Danish meget. Doublet of mye.

Pronunciation

  • IPA(key): /ˈmeːɡət/

Adverb

meget

  1. very (used with adjectives/adverbs in the positive degree)
    Synonym: veldig
  2. (archaic) alternative form of mye: much, a lot (used with verbs and adjectives/adverbs in the comparative degree)

Pronoun

meget

  1. (archaic) alternative form of mye

See also

  • ovleg (Nynorsk)

References

  • “meget” in The Bokmål Dictionary.
